### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | Journal follows Cambridge University Press's general AI ethics policy (publisher-level, not CJP-specific). AI/LLM tools may not be listed as authors. Mandatory disclosure required when AI is used to generate text/images (incl. translation) or to analyze/extract insights from data — declaration must include tool name, version, dates of use, and description of use, placed in acknowledgments/footnotes/methods/figure captions as appropriate. Basic spelling/grammar checking, single-word/brief-phrase suggestions, and minor formatting do NOT require declaration. No outright ban found; use is permitted with transparency obligations, so treated as conditional/moderate leniency rather than fully open. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/canadian-journal-of-philosophy/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** General analytic philosophy journal (any area of philosophy, published in French or English). Recent issue (Vol. 55, Issue 3, 2026) clustered around philosophy of mind/self-consciousness: an author-meets-critics symposium on Matthew Boyle's work on transparency and self-knowledge, plus a précis-and-commentary symposium on Anil Gomes's 'The Practical Self.' Format mix includes regular research articles, short discussion notes (max 3,000 words) responding to previously published articles, special issues, and author-meets-critics symposia.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** analytic philosophical argumentation / conceptual analysis, discussion notes replying to previously published CJP articles, author-meets-critics symposia (précis + multiple commentaries + reply), special issues on topics of current philosophical interest
